items.note: CHI system paper: user study (N=16) compares the CreativeConnect generative-AI recombination tool with a baseline system without generative pipelines on graphic design ideation; outcomes are number of design ideas (count on output) plus self-reported creativity; well under 50 participants, and same work as arXiv 2312.11949.

CHI extended abstract: user study (N=8) compares Expandora (LLM prompt variations for text-to-image exploration) with a baseline; outcomes are prompt diversity, number of prompts tried, and satisfaction, so the measured diversity is of prompts within a user rather than rated creativity of outputs; tiny sample; same work as arXiv 2503.00791.

AOM proceedings abstract: 2 (AI- vs colleague-generated example ideas) x 2 (early vs late exposure) between-subjects online experiment, 233 participants, scenario-based idea generation; ideas scored on novelty and feasibility; AI-versus-human-examples contrast (ideas_supplied, ai_vs_active); proceedings abstract only, full paper may not exist.

AOM proceedings abstract: two experiments vary the timing of generative-AI use (early vs late) in idea generation; novelty and feasibility of ideas are the outcomes; sample sizes and comparison to a no-AI arm not stated; likely same research group as c747 (Chung, Kim).

Conference poster (no abstract; read the poster PDF): 100 participants did the Forward Association Task and 101 the Divergent Association Task, each first solo then with an AI agent (fixed order, apparently not randomized), with AUT and semantic fluency measured pre and post; collaborative rounds more original and less variable, post-collaboration AUT fluency up and originality down; within-person pre/post design without a no-AI control group, so eligibility is doubtful.

Randomized in-person experiment: undergraduates write an analytical essay with or without generative AI, then write unaided one week later; abstract reports essay quality (style, relevance), and search notes say essay pairwise similarity was also tested (null homogenization); analytical essay may fall outside the creative-task definition; co-authored by the atlas owner (Reyes), so flag for conflict of interest.

AOM proceedings abstract: a series of lab experiments with entrepreneurs vary the level of AI usage and prior sector knowledge; AI constrains creativity and novelty in opportunity recognition; the AI tool is not named (may not be generative AI) and how creativity is measured and sample sizes are not stated.

Abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Crossref, Semantic Scholar elided by publisher, Europe PMC, Springer page): per search notes 119 participants wrote a 25-minute open-ended response with a plain word processor or with Google Smart Compose; Smart Compose is an LLM-based inline suggestion tool but may be judged predictive text (out of scope); whether creativity or similarity outcomes exist is unconfirmed.

Novice and expert designers created UI/UX designs with Galileo AI or Figma; design creativity scored with the Creative Product Semantic Scale (Figma higher), plus NASA-TLX and completion time; group assignment and sample sizes not stated in the abstract; title is truncated in the registry.

CHI paper: qualitative studies with fashion design apprentices compare a graphical design-space exploration tool (generative.fashion) with a text-prompt Stable Diffusion interface, plus two follow-up quantitative studies; an AI-configuration comparison (ai_design), but whether outputs are scored for creativity and the sample sizes are not stated; likely small.
